Hey /v/KDE, I just installed Kubuntu for the first time in my life about half an hour ago. I've been a linux user for a long time, but I've never used KDE (always with Unity, Mate or Cinnamon). I heard done tell that KDE is a robust environment but I haven't done any poking under the hood as of yet.

That being said, you folks that have been in KDE for a while, what are my must-have applications to make this the ultimate desktop experience for me?
First time KDE user, give me all your tips (but just the tips... wait.)

• Get used to krunner, <alt><f2> in KDE4, <alt><space> in Plasma5. Works great as application starter...but is so much more. Try a <alt><space>"dd:Plasma5" and you get a duckduckGo search for the term plasma5 in your browsers. "gg:<searchterm>" for google. "man:<manpage>" to open a manpage and in case your distro didn't butcher it "info:<infopage>" for gnu infopages. Any filepath in Krunner will open the filemanager at that place. "35°C" will give you a temperature in Fahrenheit, works for most other units as well. Calculations work as well: "sqrt(2)*7.8=" (= at the end it what makes krunner display the result). Switching between window by typing the window name here....really...just try it out, you can do so very much with Krunner

  • Assign shortcuts to programs. In systemsettings you can create global shortcuts...having something like <left-windows>+<c> to start a shell or <left-windows>+<d> to start dolphin can be very, very nice.

  • Install yakuake...really no clue how anyone can work without it.

  • Spend some time with widget management....and really play with it. Get a feeling for KDE there and how it's different. (Like, taskbars being just widget containers that you can customize how you want or that the desktop can be set to different widget layouts to provide something for every taste)

  • KIO. In a way I mentioned parts of that already with Krunner...but there is a lot more. Any KDE program will allow you opening remote files through sftp by typing "sftp://username:password@example.org/directory/filename" in the open file dialog, works similar for samba shares, ftp....many, many protocols. (And just for the fun of it...a "man://man" in the open file dialog of kwrite opens the generated html code for the man-manpage in kwrite...can't think of any use-case for it...but a good example how it works)

  • Kwin-window rules. For any program open the window menu with <alt><f3>, navigate to "More actions" and there you can set up special rules for programs or windows. Try it out...there are endless options. For example for blender I have global desktop shortcuts disabled as <f12> usually opens yakuake for me but is needed in blender to render a picture. (very useful for for games as well...never accidentally <alt><tab>ing out of a game). But being able to set the exact position and size...or disabling compositing even for windowed programs as soon as they are started for sure have use cases as well

  • If you are into development give KDevelop a try...it's pretty amazing (But sadly suffering a bit under the KDE4/Plasma5 transition in some distros like arch..will be hopefully solved in a few months)

  • Enjoy Konsole....and some of it's built in functions you otherwise only get with external tools like tmux (Splitting the view can be pretty useful)

  • KSysguard: System monitor that can display...about everything and even works for remote monitoring of other computers.

  • If you have an android phone...give KDEConnect a try. Fun...and very, very useful for phone/desktop integration

  • In general...look at the KDE programs even if your distro doesn't install them by default. KDE tools like marble or cantor don't really have many opensource program that can compete with them.

  • Kate: If you are into vim turn on the vim input mode for kate, if you like eye-candy enable the text preview in the scrollbar..and i general enjoy a very, very good text editor.

  • A lot of KDE programs can make use of other KDE programs...just because I mentioned kate..in fact it's more a editor component used by the kate program, kwrite but also kdevelop. Marble can be integrated in calligra office for map views, cantor integrates a lot other maths tools in one interface, kontact integrates all PIM applications in one interface...I mention this because it is not always obvious why installing something can help out in seemingly unrelated places. Without marble you simply have no option to integrate map data in calligra...it will still work normal you just miss out some additional options that would be possible.

  • Modify your desktop to your linkings! That is what KDE is about. Don't assume things are fixed...the stupid pop-up message every time you get a mail annoys you? Just turn it of in the notification settings. You would rather have a pop-up notification than just the flag icon changing if you switch keyboard layout...just change it. You don't see the use of a start-menu with Krunner? Why do you still have it then..just remove it.

  • Learn some shortcuts. <alt><rightclick> to resize windows is great, <alt><leftclick> to move them as well. If you miss something have a look if you can set it..in the majority of cases you can set the shortcut as you want for programs...in fact only a tiny minority of shortcuts are set by default in KDE..the much large part is just there and waits to get a key assigned.

  • Install kipi-plugins to have options like uploading to image sharing sites right from within ksnapshot or gwenview...together with some image filters.

  • <f4> in dolphin...sorry, important enough to know to justify an own point
